utterances.text: The policeman told us that soldiers of the HVO wearing HVO insignia broke into these buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go back to Valenta a bit. Valenta spoke about the first meeting, the reasons for setting up the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. You told us about that in the morning so I am interested in hearing whether at any point he said that Herceg-Bosna would secede from Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would it secede?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, did he announce that; did he say that was the objective?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember him saying that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: there was a Crisis Staff, you said, in Vitez of the Vitez municipality. Were there crisis staffs of local communities or villages as lower organisational units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was something to that effect at local community level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how many local communities there were, how many crisis staffs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not really know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, in 1992, when these crisis staffs were established, could the Crisis Staff of the local community use their own soldiers at their own discretion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So such things never happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because the army had their own command, and the Crisis Staff could use them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean of the municipality and nobody else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am interested in hearing whether you know which body set up the HVO government in Vitez. How was the HVO government in Vitez set up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the civilian HVO or HDZ offered to you in Vitez -- I mean to you, representatives of the Muslim people -- a division of power according to the results of the elections in 1990, subjecting all the armed forces to a joint authority and also setting up a joint army in proportion to the number of units and working according to the decrees of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Why were these terms unacceptable for you, or rather, were some acceptable and others unacceptable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was unacceptable to us the heading itself, because we thought that in Vitez we could not have a single nation government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But would that not be a multinational government if the results of the elections from 1990 would have been respected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In its very name it is a single nation government, the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move on to the Co-ordinating Committee for the Protection of Muslims now. Could you tell us who launched this initiative to set up this Co-ordinating Committee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Executive Committee of the SDA party convened a meeting of all members of the other Parliamentary parties and prominent persons, business people of Bosniak nationality from Vitez. At this meeting, which was a large meeting, the decision was reached to set up a Co-ordinating Committee for Protecting the Interests of Muslims in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me now -- can you remember who was elected then to this Co-ordinating Committee, these 19 names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The President of the Co-ordinating Committee for Protecting the Interests of Muslims was Fuad Kaknjo, the President of the municipal government. Munib Kajmovic was a member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember: what was Munib Kajmovic in charge of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what he was in charge of. I can just enumerate the members. I know that I was supposed to monitor health, and I can enumerate the members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, let us hear the members.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Salibasic Hasan, an economist; Salkic Suad, an electrical engineer; Seco Fuad, veterinarian from Vitez; Kalco Nusret, a mechanical engineer from Vitez, a member of the SDP, and Salkic Suad is a member of the reformists; Sivro Hasim, a member of the Youth League.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sivro Hasim or Sivro Bahtija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both Sivro Hasim and Sivro Bahtija. Krajic Cazim, a private entrepreneur; Kovacevic Halil, a private entrepreneur; Vitkic Sulejman, a private entrepreneur; Cazim Ahmic, he is an engineer of organisation; Ahmic Sulejman, an economist. I cannot remember anyone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I could read it out to you and if you agree, please tell me and if not you can deny it. For economic affairs, was Nusret Kalco in charge of that? What did he do otherwise; tell me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is a mechanical engineer in the work organisation Vitezit. He was Deputy Director General for finance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hasan Salibasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is an economist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that he was in charge of finance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know; I think he was, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what is he by professional training and where did he work?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is it that important for you, Mr. Nobilo? Are these questions important for you? Okay, because we have a lot about this Commission for the Protection of Muslims and about the members, but I would like to remind you that it is 5.30, and we will end the hearing after you complete this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I suggest then that we conclude now, because I would like to continue my questioning on the co-ordinating committee. I said that I suggest that we conclude now, because I have quite a bit of questioning left on this co-ordinating committee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, but please think about the time you need in view of the time taken by the Prosecutor, so you will tell us tomorrow morning roughly how much time you need for your cross-examination, both of you, Mr. Nobilo and Mr. Hayman. Very well, the meeting is adjourned. It will be resumed tomorrow at 10.00. (5.35 pm) (Court adjourned until 10.00 am the following day) 23 24 25
